DSIR

Data Science Infrastructure for Global Health

From Global Health Data to Clear Insights

DSIR is an open-source R package that simplifies access to global health data, supports consistent data processing, and provides reusable tools for analysis and visualization.

Explore Features Get Started

Technical Overview → GitHub →

Open source · Available on CRAN · MIT licence

The everyday challenge

Why DSIR?

Health data are spread across platforms, with different table structures and geographical identifiers. Analysts repeatedly retrieve, clean and format data, while keeping their work reproducible and their reports consistent.

DSIR brings commonly used global health data sources and analytical utilities into a consistent R workflow, reducing repetitive data preparation and supporting reproducible analyses.

For technical teams preparing country comparisons, monitoring indicators and producing public health reports.

What you can do

Core capabilities

01 / ACCESS

Access Global Health Data

Retrieve observations from WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO), WHO Global Health Estimates (GHE), and UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) services. Select countries, years and population breakdowns.

Explore WHO data access →

02 / PREPARE

Harmonize Data

Work with a consistent cleaned table structure, WHO Member State metadata and country identifiers. Keep additional dimensions and source information when needed.

See data preparation tools →

03 / ANALYSE

Analyse Health Indicators

Use life tables, direct age standardization and measures of annual progress to support mortality analysis and indicator monitoring.

Explore analytical methods →

04 / PRESENT

Visualize and Present Results

Apply reusable ggplot2 themes and flextable formatting to create consistent charts and analytical tables for technical reports.

View visualization examples →

A common table structure does not make indicator definitions or estimation methods comparable. Check source methods, population breakdowns and units before comparing results.

From tools to tasks

Practical applications

For WHO technical teams and public health researchers working with international health data.

  • Monitor health indicators

    Explore observations across countries and years, keeping population groups and data sources visible.

  • Explore mortality and disease burden

    Examine WHO estimates by cause, age, sex, country and year.

  • Assess progress towards SDG targets

    Retrieve health-related SDG series and analyse changes over time.

  • Prepare reproducible reports

    Reuse data preparation steps, charts and table styles across analytical outputs.

These are potential uses of the package, not claims of official adoption by WHO.

Ongoing development

Development roadmap

DSIR continues to evolve in response to practical needs in global health data analysis. Future development is planned to include GIS-related functions to support geospatial data processing, mapping and spatial analysis.

GIS capabilities are a future direction and are not part of the current release.

Start with the package

Getting started

Install DSIR from CRAN, then follow the technical guide for data access, analysis and presentation. 

install.packages("DSIR")
library(DSIR)
